verdict_reason: The pointwise estimator is exactly Ma et al. Eq. 4: it matched the fetched reference expression with maximum relative error 0 and matched full direct-distance summaries exactly on an ordinary cloud. It is not fully scale/translation invariant numerically: rescaling a cloud by 1e-11 changes mean LID 17.0221 into no estimate, and translating another valid cloud changes the direct mean 28.8354 to 20.9075 (-27.49%).
comparable_reason: The main summaries are not dominated by architecture in the 46-model table: lid_mean has rho=0.164 with width and 0.130 with depth, while lid_median is moderately associated at rho=0.374 and 0.338. Zero-padding a fixed cloud from width 32 to 512 leaves lid_mean bit-identical, so ambient width is not algebraically forced; nevertheless lid_min correlates with vocab_size at rho=0.650 and all cross-model uses need size controls.
github_reason: The authors' util.py was fetched and its mle_batch expression was run on identical neighbor lists: k is capped at len(data)-1 and each value is -k/sum(log(v/v[-1])) after self exclusion. BLME matched pointwise with maximum relative error 0 and matched mean 19.877423772242715 and median 19.330263899640656 on a 400x32 cloud (median difference 1.1e-14).
paper_reason: Ma et al. publish detector AUCs, not raw LID summaries for released coordinates, and their illustrative LID plot is not accompanied by the underlying points. There is no directly reproducible paper number for this quantity; analytic uniform-ball checks produced medians 2.132, 4.977, 9.260, and 16.631 for true dimensions 2, 5, 10, and 20.
confounds_reason: Across 46 model rows, lid_mean correlations with d_model/n_layers/vocab_size are 0.164/0.130/-0.221, while lid_median gives 0.374 (p=0.0105)/0.338 (p=0.0217)/-0.281. The estimator is exactly invariant to zero-padding in a controlled cloud, but lid_min has rho=0.650 with vocab_size; the family shows associations without evidence that the main mean is mechanically a width proxy.
defects: src/blme/tasks/geometry/lid.py:40-42 applies an absolute distance cutoff. A scale-invariant cloud with mean LID 17.022135 at unit scale returns no estimate after multiplication by 1e-11.

src/blme/tasks/geometry/lid.py:102-135 uses the Gram identity to select only k+9 candidates. On a translated but otherwise unchanged 700x48 cloud, candidate mis-selection changes mean LID from the exact 28.835392 to 20.907541 (-27.49%); the previously claimed 1e5 counterexample is refuted, as that case matches exactly.

src/blme/tasks/geometry/lid.py:137-143 drops zero estimates that the released mle_batch retains. On a cloud with 200 duplicate-query cases out of 400, the official aggregate mean is 10.706151 while BLME reports 21.412302 over only the positive half.

The cache path at lid.py:197-200 uses all cached tokens, while the fresh single-layer collector samples at most 10 tokens per document at geometry/utils.py:204-210, so cache state changes the evaluated population.

Single-layer mode uses the post-final-normalization hidden state while layerwise keys are described as layer outputs; this is a defined representation but needs an explicit layer identity in provenance.
fix: Replace absolute distance guards with scale-relative tests; detect unreliable Gram candidate ordering and widen candidates or fall back to direct blockwise distances; decide and document whether reference-zero duplicate estimates belong in aggregates and report excluded counts; and make cache/fresh token sampling identical.
